sermon.title: Is God's Presence Enough?
sermon.speaker: Michael Silla
sermon.summary: God’s presence brings joy, but is it enough? Saul and Samson had His Spirit upon them yet didn’t obey. Joseph listened and was exalted. Elijah heard the still small voice. Jesus told Peter to feed His sheep. Eternal life is knowing God—hearing and responding.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear.

chunks.short_answer: God spoke light and it was; rocks cry out if we don’t praise; Elijah gave up in fear—praise God for people who messed up.
chunks.text:
Going back to the beginning, Genesis 1:3, God said, “Let there be light.” And there was light. And God saw the light that it was good. And God divided the light from the darkness. And he called the light day and the darkness he called night. So the evening and morning were the first day. His g his presence was wonderful and powerful hovering over the face of the waters. But nothing happened until g until God spoke. We know this. When God spoke, creation responded. All of the things that were there that started to respond to God’s word. I wish us humans would act like that. But of course, God’s creation, they don’t have a choice.

They got to respond. The rocks will cry out if you don’t if you guys don’t praise. The rocks are going to cry out. In Joshua 24:14, it [clears throat] says, “Choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve.” We have a choice. Are we going to listen to God’s word and choose to follow it? Many people today have chosen not to serve the Lord. And many think it evil to serve him because he judges and because he says no. It’s kind of like our police force today. Police have to enforce the law. They got to tell the criminal no. They got to say they got to put them in the car when they’re bad, right?

It’s the same with God. He’s got to tell us no so people don’t like him. Psalm 138:2, I will worship toward your holy temple. Praise and praise your name for your loving kindness. For you have magnified your word above all your name. His presence in his presence is fullness of joy. But without his word, we’re not going to grow and we’re not going to know God. His word is above his name. His word is above his presence. The word is most important. Elijah, going back to Elijah, after the fire, a still small voice. And uh going back to that story, there came a still small voice.

He had just experienced an earthquake, a tornado, a fire, all these things happening. Whoa. Wow. Look at those miracles. But Elijah heard the still small voice and then he came out and God a voice came to him and said what are you doing here Elijah now you if you don’t know God had already asked him this question and he asked him this question this is the second time he asked the question and this is the second time Elijah gives the same response he says I have been zealous for the Lord because the children have forsaken your covenant, torn down your altars, killed your prophets with the sword, and I al am left and they seek to take my life. See, Elijah was in a give up mode.

He was giving up. He was in the scared mode. He was afraid. He was in the there’s no way we can overcome this mode. And it’s easy to get in that mode. You get scared. There’s a that the enemy looks too big. [clears throat] But we can’t do that. We’ve got to trust in what? The word of God. And when you think about that question, what are you doing here? He said it twice, right? It’s not like God doesn’t know. God knows why you’re there. What he’s saying is you shouldn’t be here. What are you doing here? This is not where you should be. You should be listening to my voice.

And you know what? Praise God for people in the Bible that messed up. My goodness. I mean, we’ve all been in this spot where we didn’t respond right, where we’re where we are where we shouldn’t be. Amen. And God gives us an opportunity to respond again. And he says to Elijah, he doesn’t go into all of his statements and his uh feelings and all that. He just says, “Go return.” I mean, a couple words here. Go and return. You shouldn’t be here. And he tells him what to do. Go and do this and go and do that. And Elijah gets up and he goes and he does it. So he responded right. Do we respond right? It might take us a long time but you know if it takes you a long time at least you’re get down get moving in his path and following his voice.

chunks.section_question: What do Lazarus and Peter teach?
chunks.short_answer: Martha objected but Jesus did His will; Jesus told Peter feed My sheep, follow Me.
chunks.text:
Amen. Jesus and Lazarus John 11:39. [clears throat] So he had just said take away the stone. And Martha replies and says, ‘Lord, by this time there’s a stench. And Jesus said, ‘D did I not say to you? Of course, they had a conversation before about him being the resurrection and life. Did I not say to you that I would if you would believe, you would see the glory of God? Jesus lifted up his eyes and he says, “Father, I thank you for you. You have heard me. Everybody else, they didn’t hear me. Right? And sometimes it’s hard for us to hear God. Sometimes Jesus is saying things and it’s like, well, that’s never happened before.

How could you do that? What do you mean? Right? It takes like five or 10, maybe a hundred times before it gets in. But Jesus and God, they know what’s going on. I thank you for you have heard me. And you always hear me.” [clears And of course, throat] when he cried out with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come forth.” Lazarus got up, his face was wrapped with with cloth, and Jesus said to him, “Loose him and let him go.” And so we see here that his presence wasn’t the key to Lazarus coming out of the grave. It was when he spoke. And even though people did not understand, God still did.

Jesus still did his will. And thank God sometimes we don’t understand. And Jesus still does what he needs to do. But we do want to understand. How many you know it would have been better for Martha and Mary to understand at that time and to be glad. God, we know you’re going to do a great work right now and you’re going to share. You’re going to show these folks how wonderful and awesome you are. You’re going to show them that you’re God. See, that could have been their response, right? And uh it would have been good. And we want to have that response. But if you have the kind of response they do, When you understand, just get on the train, right? Get on the train of God’s voice and his word.

Jesus and his disciples, as we had spoken before in John 20, he came into the room and he showed them his body. He showed them his hands and his feet. He and they were glad when they saw him. And how many of you would be glad when you if you saw Jesus? I would be very glad. He had just uh rose. My goodness, I’d love to see him. And Jesus in the room while he’s having them and showing him his them his body, he says to them, “As the father has sent me, I also send you.” And he breathed on them and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit.” And they received the spirit. And he sent them at that time. And then what happened later, the next chapter 21:3, Peter says, “I’m going to go fishing.” And they said to him, “We’re going to go with you.” Right?

Uh was was James and John there? Who was who was with Peter? Who’s who’s we? I’m not testing. I’m wondering. I don’t remember. I think it was James and John. John, the one you know who loved God, loved Jesus, was also fishing. And he says, Jesus says to Peter, “Simon, do you love me?” So, of course, you know, he calls him out from the boat. Peter realizes that it’s Jesus and he jumps into the water, meets Jesus on land. They catch a bunch of fish. You know that backstory. But Jesus says to Peter, “Do you love me more than these?” Again, here we have a case where God spoke it already. Right? He send He said, “I send you. Here’s my spirit.” And Peter, James, and John, they go fishing.

The fish don’t need you. God didn’t send you to the fish. He sent you to mankind. So they didn’t hear it the first time, right? So God, thank goodness before he ascends, he’s he’s like, “Okay, these guys, they didn’t get it the first time. They’re fishing. I mean, it’s a beautiful day. They’re not catching anything because I I don’t have the fish near the boat for a reason.” No, I’m just kidding. But they didn’t hear it the first time. So he brings them, they’re eating, and he says, “Simon, do you love me?” And he replies, says, “Yes, Lord. You know that I love you. Feed my lambs.” And of course, he asked the question three times.

And his reply was, “Feed my lambs. Tend my sheep. Feed my sheep.” And then he says at the end, follow me. So somewhere along the lines, the disciples get the message and they were told to go wait in Jerusalem until power be until the uh comforter comes, spirit of God. And so they did that. So they finally we we’re on the right train, right? We heard it two or three times. It didn’t get in the first time. Now we hear it and we’re responding. My goodness. If it takes you 20, if it takes you a hundred times, how many however many times it takes you, it’d be nice if you listened the first time. If we sorry listen the first time, but if it takes you a few more, just have a heart that responds to Christ.

If it’s if it’s because you don’t understand, then seek understanding. If you understand it, but you reject it, you got a problem. If you understand it and you ignore it, you got a problem. But we’ve got to respond and take his word seriously. So God is asking us this morning, what will we do? The presence of God is very powerful. The spirit being upon us is very powerful. It’s powerful when he comes in worship with his presence and he touches and he moves upon us. But God is wanting more out of the church today in America and all over the world. He wants us to grow and he wants us to know him.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of him who was dead, said to Him, “Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days.”

So when they had eaten breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love Me more than these?” He said to Him, “Yes, Lord; You know that I love You.” He said to him, “Feed My lambs.” He said to him again a second time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love Me?” He said to Him, “Yes, Lord; You know that I love You.” He said to him, “Tend My sheep.” He said to him the third time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love Me?” Peter was grieved because He said to him the third time, “Do you love Me?” And he said to Him, “Lord, You know all things; You know that I love You.” Jesus said to him, “Feed My sheep. Most assuredly, I say to you, when you were younger, you girded yourself and walked where you wished; but when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you and carry you where you do not wish.” This He spoke, signifying by what death he would glorify God. And when He had spoken this, He said to him, “Follow Me.”

chunks.short_answer: To know God—hear His voice and ask, “What’s next?”; do we have an ear to hear?
chunks.text:
He says in again in John chapter 17, this is eternal life. To know God and to know God, we have to hear his voice. And we’ve got to respond in obedience. Are we listening beyond the presence of God? Do we just come to be in that joy and then leave? I remember experiences experiencing this as a young uh teenager. Uh it was so wonderful as a 12-year-old. Uh they let me into the teen service and uh I experienced God for the first time and there was some rascals around me and uh but we all responded and came down. And I remember there was a particular rascal who was right next to me experiencing the same thing and we were both crying and and just experiencing the presence of God for the first time and uh God was just so powerful that day and I wanted more of that and I was like how do I get more of this?

And for, you know, I would be I would go to church with mom and dad and we’d sit in Carbon Canyon and we worship and I would lift my hands and I would feel God’s presence. I’m like, “Wow, that’s wonderful.” But it didn’t last very long. I would say by the time I was 14, I was like, “What? What happened? I don’t feel what I used to feel.” Because we’ve got to go beyond just the feeling. We’ve got to go beyond just the joy that comes. Are we listening? And that’s exactly what it caused me to do. I was like, “Dad, what’s going on?” And I started asking questions and I started saying, “What am I doing?

What do I got to do now?” That’s what God wants you to do. What’s next? You can’t just be a a bozo. Just kidding. How do we respond to God’s voice? Does it take us too many times or we already went over that if it takes you 100 times just and it doesn’t get in? It just takes a hundred times. Are we willing to be obedient? And this is the key as s as Samuel said to Saul, God is more interested in our obedience. As a worship team comes says in John 11:15, he who has an ear to hear, let him hear what the spirit is saying to the churches.

It says in Revelation, and God is looking and asking for his people, do we have an ear to hear? Do we have an ear like Joseph? He was able to interpret the dream. Do we have an hearing ear? Unlike Martha and Mary? Do we have an ear that hears what God is saying? In Matthew 28:1 19 says, “Go therefore make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all the things I’ve commanded. And God, I and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Are we willing to be obedient this morning? And after this morning, let’s bow our heads this morning. Let’s just invite Jesus right now.

faqs.question: Why did Joseph have to be sold?
faqs.answer: So the butler could tell Pharaoh about him.

faqs.question: How many times before it gets in?
Does he remember who was with Peter?
Who did God send you to?
Where did he worship as a kid?
faqs.answer: Carbon Canyon with mom and dad.
